rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child's central budgetary explanation. Both letters answer congressional concern about large federal spending by distinguishing current-year cash expenditures from much larger appropriations or obligational authority whose outlays occur in later years, emphasizing prior cost review, and arguing that essential security programs cannot safely be reduced merely because their headline authorization is large. C07 closely parallels the child's treatment of Mutual Security funding, lead-time financing, prior rescreening, and the danger of major cuts, while C13 parallels the government-wide reexamination and proposed deferral of lower-priority public works. C15 is strongest because its appropriations-versus-expenditures distinction structures a substantial portion of the later letter rather than supplying only one program-specific point.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the 1958 budget...is in effect two budgets within one. One consists of requests for new spending authority...The other concerns the actual expenditures of the agencies in the next fiscal year.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: While appropriations of nearly 3.1 billion dollars are needed in the fiscal year 1953...it is estimated that actual expenditures in that year will amount to only about 650 million dollars; the remainder will need to be obligated...until subsequent years.
shared_material.explanation: Both distinguish authority or appropriations from current fiscal-year expenditures and explain that much of the authorized amount produces cash outlays only in later years.

shared_material.child_excerpt: painstaking efforts were made in preparing the budget to pare to the minimum all projected expenditures and programs
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The program has been carefully reviewed in order to bring its total cost down to a practicable minimum. Every effort has been made to exclude facilities not essential
shared_material.explanation: The later letter reuses the same reviewed-to-a-minimum justification before resisting deeper reductions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: a cut of any appreciable consequence in current expenditures for national security and related programs would endanger our country and the peace of the world
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The cost of the expansion program will be substantial. We must nevertheless continue our efforts to buttress the security of this country and of the free world. Not to do so invites disaster.
shared_material.explanation: Both pair fiscal restraint with an argument that substantial reductions in essential security expenditures would be dangerous.
